newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin agrees to have heart operation - RIA agency.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin agrees to have heart operation - RIA agency.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has agreed to have a heart operation, RIA news agency said on Thursday.
RIA said the operation was likely to take place at the end of September in Moscow.

Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as telling RIA television in an interview that the doctors who had established that Yeltsin had heart problems had given him a choice -- have an operation or "work passively".

"B. Yeltsin said that passive work has never suited him. That is why he has decided to recover fully through an operation," the agency said. It did not say what kind of operation the president, 65, needed.

Yeltsin said he was not going to have an operation outside Russia. "Our cardiological centre is capable of conducting such operations. I think it is fitting for the president to have an operation in the motherland," he said. "I hope for support from the Russians."

Yeltsin, who had two heart attacks last year, had disappeared from public view on June 26. Aides had so far denied that he was ill, saying only that the president was exhausted after a gruelling election campaign.
